domain: domain-configuration/pipeline — the CDM pipeline router (/p0/cdm/pipeline/*), shared by every stage

verifiedAgainst.note: All 7 paths, methods, and parameter PLACEMENTS below are read straight from the live OpenAPI document, not inferred. Response bodies are NOT documented there — every 2xx declares `content: {application/json: {schema: {}}}` — so response shapes are marked confirmed only where a real payload was supplied.

proxyRoute.note: One catch-all already covers all 7 endpoints — no new route files were needed.

stageEnum.evidence: RunPipelineRequest.stage carries the literal regex `^(sap|docs|ts|pnid|aif|gloc|lopc|full)$` in the live spec.
stageEnum.correctionHistory: An earlier pass asked the user whether `aif|gloc|lopc` were real, working only from an ambiguous pasted table whose prose and bullet list disagreed; the answer given was 'only sap/pnid/ts/docs/full'. The live spec CONTRADICTS that answer — all 8 are valid. Corroborated in-app: admin.constants.js already defines FEED_TYPES = ['AIF','GLOC','LOPC'] and keys.js documents seven connectors including them. Trust this entry, not the earlier Q&A.
stageEnum.uiCoverage: aif/gloc/lopc upload through the connectors flow but have no review screen, so no UI triggers those stages yet (see DataConfigView.jsx's REVIEW_VIEW_BY_TYPE comment). The service accepts them; only the 4 stages in PIPELINE_ROWS are wired to the run UI.

endpoints.serviceFunction: runPipeline({ stage, plant_code_id, incremental = false, industry?, file_names?, doc_types?, doc_files?, upload_batch_id? })
endpoints.description: Start a CDM pipeline stage asynchronously. Returns a pipeline_job_id to poll.

queryParams.value: NONE — the live spec declares `parameters: []` for this operation.
queryParams.note: The previous implementation also sent plant_code_id as a query param 'for back-compat'. Removed: the endpoint declares no query params, so it could never have been read there. Body-only, per RunPipelineRequest.

plant_code_id.note: Rule 0. Backend defaults to its seed plant if omitted — always pass the real selected plant.

industry.note: cement | oil_gas. Falls back to user_config.yaml if omitted.

incremental.note: If true, merge with existing output instead of overwrite. Service defaults it to false so no caller has to know it exists.

file_names.note: pnid stage: PDFs uploaded this session. docs stage (legacy): doc_type keys — prefer doc_types.

doc_types.note: docs stage: explicit document_type keys (sop, rca_reports, …).

doc_files.note: docs stage: filenames uploaded this session; already-processed files are tracked in {work_dir}/docs_done.json and skipped.

upload_batch_id.note: Opaque batch id stamped on every processed row so the review API can scope to exactly this run. If omitted the pipeline_job_id is used as the batch id (recommended — one run == one reviewable batch).

responseBody.confirmed: shape supplied by the user; NOT in the spec (schema is empty)

data.stages_planned: Array<{ phase, label, weight, determinate, file_wise? }> — full planned stage list, so a stepper can render before the first poll
data.is_determinate: boolean — false => UI must show an indeterminate bar

consumedBy: usePipelineOrchestration.js#triggerPipeline → usePipelineRuns#registerRun (stages_planned / is_determinate / files_total / progress_percent seed the run row before the first poll)
usePipelineOrchestration.js commitDocsContext / commitTsContext / commitSapContext (fire-and-forget follow-up runs)

endpoints.description: Poll the status of a running or completed pipeline job.

responseBody.previouslyConfirmedFields: { pipeline_job_id, stage, plant_code_id, upload_batch_id, status, output_tables, record_counts, total_records }
responseBody.status: queued | running | completed | failed | cancelled (+ partial / interrupted, named by the retry endpoint's own description)
responseBody.expectedButUNCONFIRMED: progress_percent, is_determinate, stages[], counters{files_total,files_done}, current_stage, current_item. POST /run now returns the planned/determinacy fields, so the runtime equivalents are very likely present here too — but the endpoint is auth-gated (401 'Missing session' without a live browser token) so this could not be verified from the CLI.
responseBody.howTheCodeHandlesThat: pipelineRun.utils.js#derivePipelineProgress reads progress_percent first, then falls back to a weight-based roll-up of stages[], then returns null — and null renders an honest indeterminate bar instead of a number. So the UI is correct whether or not the backend supplies these.

endpoints.consumedBy: usePipelineQueries.js#usePipelineJobPolls (useQueries — polls all active stages in parallel, 3s, refetchIntervalInBackground: true so minimised/background runs keep progressing)

endpoints.description: SIGTERM the pipeline subprocess AND its whole process group (so the LLM extractor / Bedrock calls stop too); SIGKILL after 5s. Marks the job `cancelled`. No-op 200 if the job already finished.

responseBody.note: Undocumented. The UI does not read it — it invalidates the job poll and lets the next poll report `cancelled`.

endpoints.consumedBy: usePipelineQueries.js#useCancelPipelineJob → usePipelineRuns#cancelRun → usePipelineRunView#requestCancel (always behind the shared ConfirmDialog)
endpoints.uxNotes: Because the endpoint is a no-op 200 on an already-finished job, cancelRun deliberately does NOT force status to 'cancelled' locally — a cancel that races a completion must keep the real result.

endpoints.description: List all recent pipeline jobs, newest first. Optionally filter by stage.

responseBody.observed: array of job objects; fields have appeared as pipeline_job_id|job_id and plant_code_id|plant_code, plus an optional `warning: { reason, category, evidence }`
responseBody.note: normalizePipelineJob() in the service reconciles the id/batch aliases so no consumer re-guesses them.

endpoints.consumedBy: data-activity/activityService.js#getPipelineJobs → useDataActivityQueries#usePipelineJobs. This endpoint used to be declared a SECOND time inside activityService with its own param spelling; that duplicate was removed (2026-08-17) and activityService now delegates to listPipelineJobs, keeping only its own table-presentation mapping.

endpoints.description: Re-run a failed / partial / cancelled / interrupted job with the same stage and plant.

scope.note: failed_only re-runs just the files that did not succeed; all re-runs everything the original job covered.

responseBody.note: Assumed to mirror POST /run (a NEW pipeline_job_id). usePipelineRuns#retryRun reads pipeline_job_id || job_id and re-registers the run under that new id; if neither is present it bails rather than polling a stale job.

endpoints.consumedBy: usePipelineQueries.js#useRetryPipelineJob → usePipelineRuns#retryRun → the retry button on PipelineRunRow (shown only for retryable terminal statuses)

endpoints.description: List all CSV files in the CDM output directory, grouped by stage. plant_code_id scopes to that plant's cdm_out subtree (required now that output is plant-segregated).
endpoints.consumedBy: NOTHING YET — service function only, no query hook. Adding a hook without a screen to use it would be dead code; wire one up when an outputs browser is built.

endpoints.serviceFunction: previewPipelineOutput({ stage, table, plantCode, limit = 50, offset = 0 })
endpoints.description: Return the first N rows of a CDM output CSV as JSON. Use limit and offset for pagination.

openIssues: GET /pipeline/jobs/{jobId}'s runtime progress fields (progress_percent, is_determinate, stages[], counters) remain UNCONFIRMED — the endpoint 401s ('Missing session') outside a browser session, and the spec documents no response schema. Capture one real poll payload from DevTools during a run and record it here; if the field names differ from the assumption, only pipelineRun.utils.js#derivePipelineProgress and usePipelineRuns#readRunFields need to change.
Response shapes for cancel, retry, jobs-list, and both outputs endpoints are all undocumented in the spec. Only retry's is relied upon (for the new job id), and it fails safe if absent.

The backend accepts aif/gloc/lopc stages but no UI triggers them — those three source types have no review screen, so they are uploaded and never processed. Worth confirming with the backend team whether they are expected to run via this same endpoint.
relatedRemovals: The `Math.random() * 8 + 4` fake progress bar and the Promise-wrapped setInterval poll in usePipelineOrchestration.js are gone — replaced by usePipelineRuns.js + usePipelineJobPolls. The old poll also treated only completed/failed as terminal, which would have polled a `cancelled` job forever once the cancel endpoint was wired up.
usePipelineJob + useRunPipeline in _queries/useDsiQueries.js (both consumer-less) — superseded by usePipelineQueries.js.
